From e4056b84af0fc18c84b4e5741df04ecd8ca17973 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@linaro.org>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 09:15:07 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] media: rockchip: rkcif: fix off by one bugs

Change these comparisons from > vs >= to avoid accessing one element
beyond the end of the arrays.
While at it, use ARRAY_SIZE instead of the _MAX enum values.

Fixes: 1f2353f5a1af ("media: rockchip: rkcif: add support for rk3568 vicap mipi capture")
Cc: stable@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@linaro.org>
Reviewed-by: Michael Riesch <michael.riesch@collabora.com>
Reviewed-by: Paul Elder <paul.elder@ideasonboard.com>
Reviewed-by: Laurent Pinchart <laurent.pinchart@ideasonboard.com>
Tested-by: Chen-Yu Tsai <wens@kernel.org>
[fix cosmetic issues]
Signed-off-by: Michael Riesch <michael.riesch@collabora.com>
Signed-off-by: Sakari Ailus <sakari.ailus@linux.intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Mauro Carvalho Chehab <mchehab+huawei@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/media/platform/rockchip/rkcif/rkcif-capture-mipi.c b/drivers/media/platform/rockchip/rkcif/rkcif-capture-mipi.c
index 1b81bcc067ef..9e67160a16e4 100644
--- a/drivers/media/platform/rockchip/rkcif/rkcif-capture-mipi.c
+++ b/drivers/media/platform/rockchip/rkcif/rkcif-capture-mipi.c
@@ -489,8 +489,8 @@ static inline unsigned int rkcif_mipi_get_reg(struct rkcif_interface *interface,
 
 	block = interface->index - RKCIF_MIPI_BASE;
 
-	if (WARN_ON_ONCE(block > RKCIF_MIPI_MAX - RKCIF_MIPI_BASE) ||
-	    WARN_ON_ONCE(index > RKCIF_MIPI_REGISTER_MAX))
+	if (WARN_ON_ONCE(block >= ARRAY_SIZE(rkcif->match_data->mipi->blocks)) ||
+	    WARN_ON_ONCE(index >= ARRAY_SIZE(rkcif->match_data->mipi->regs)))
 		return RKCIF_REGISTER_NOTSUPPORTED;
 
 	offset = rkcif->match_data->mipi->blocks[block].offset;
@@ -510,9 +510,9 @@ static inline unsigned int rkcif_mipi_id_get_reg(struct rkcif_stream *stream,
 	block = stream->interface->index - RKCIF_MIPI_BASE;
 	id = stream->id;
 
-	if (WARN_ON_ONCE(block > RKCIF_MIPI_MAX - RKCIF_MIPI_BASE) ||
-	    WARN_ON_ONCE(id > RKCIF_ID_MAX) ||
-	    WARN_ON_ONCE(index > RKCIF_MIPI_ID_REGISTER_MAX))
+	if (WARN_ON_ONCE(block >= ARRAY_SIZE(rkcif->match_data->mipi->blocks)) ||
+	    WARN_ON_ONCE(id >= ARRAY_SIZE(rkcif->match_data->mipi->regs_id)) ||
+	    WARN_ON_ONCE(index >= ARRAY_SIZE(rkcif->match_data->mipi->regs_id[id])))
 		return RKCIF_REGISTER_NOTSUPPORTED;
 
 	offset = rkcif->match_data->mipi->blocks[block].offset;
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

The patch fixes off-by-one bugs in the Rockchip camera interface (rkcif) MIPI capture driver, specifically in two functions that compute register offsets. Both functions used `>` comparisons against hardcoded maximum values (derived from enum constants), which allowed access one element beyond the end of the corresponding arrays. The fix replaces these comparisons with `>=` and uses the `ARRAY_SIZE()` macro for bounds checking.

### File Modified: `drivers/media/platform/rockchip/rkcif/rkcif-capture-mipi.c`

**1. Function `rkcif_mipi_get_reg`**
- Changed the `block` bounds check from:
  `block > RKCIF_MIPI_MAX - RKCIF_MIPI_BASE`
  to:
  `block >= ARRAY_SIZE(rkcif->match_data->mipi->blocks)`
- Changed the `index` bounds check from:
  `index > RKCIF_MIPI_REGISTER_MAX`
  to:
  `index >= ARRAY_SIZE(rkcif->match_data->mipi->regs)`

**2. Function `rkcif_mipi_id_get_reg`**
- Changed the `block` bounds check from:
  `block > RKCIF_MIPI_MAX - RKCIF_MIPI_BASE`
  to:
  `block >= ARRAY_SIZE(rkcif->match_data->mipi->blocks)`
- Changed the `id` bounds check from:
  `id > RKCIF_ID_MAX`
  to:
  `id >= ARRAY_SIZE(rkcif->match_data->mipi->regs_id)`
- Changed the `index` bounds check from:
  `index > RKCIF_MIPI_ID_REGISTER_MAX`
  to:
  `index >= ARRAY_SIZE(rkcif->match_data->mipi->regs_id[id])`

### Relationship Between Modifications

Both functions perform similar validation of array indices (`block`, `id`, `index`) before using them to look up register offsets from dynamically sized arrays (`blocks`, `regs`, `regs_id`). The original code used constant maximum values (`_MAX` enums) that were likely derived from the same arrays but not automatically synchronized, leading to off-by-one errors when the array sizes changed. The patch consistently switches to `ARRAY_SIZE()` for all array-index checks in both functions, ensuring correct bounds and making the code resilient to future array size modifications. The semantic change from `>` to `>=` is the core fix, while the adoption of `ARRAY_SIZE` improves maintainability and readability.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
if (WARN_ON_ONCE(block > RKCIF_MIPI_MAX - RKCIF_MIPI_BASE) ||
    WARN_ON_ONCE(index > RKCIF_MIPI_REGISTER_MAX))
if (WARN_ON_ONCE(block > RKCIF_MIPI_MAX - RKCIF_MIPI_BASE) ||
    WARN_ON_ONCE(id > RKCIF_ID_MAX) ||
    WARN_ON_ONCE(index > RKCIF_MIPI_ID_REGISTER_MAX))

Reason:
The comparisons use `>` instead of `>=`, so when `block`, `index`, or `id` equal the maximum valid index (e.g., `RKCIF_MIPI_MAX - RKCIF_MIPI_BASE`), the condition is false and the code proceeds to use them as array indices. This allows accessing one element beyond the end of the corresponding arrays, resulting in an off-by-one out-of-bounds read.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
if (WARN_ON_ONCE(block >= ARRAY_SIZE(rkcif->match_data->mipi->blocks)) ||
    WARN_ON_ONCE(index >= ARRAY_SIZE(rkcif->match_data->mipi->regs)))
if (WARN_ON_ONCE(block >= ARRAY_SIZE(rkcif->match_data->mipi->blocks)) ||
    WARN_ON_ONCE(id >= ARRAY_SIZE(rkcif->match_data->mipi->regs_id)) ||
    WARN_ON_ONCE(index >= ARRAY_SIZE(rkcif->match_data->mipi->regs_id[id])))

Reason:
The fix changes the operators from `>` to `>=`, ensuring that the condition triggers exactly when the index reaches the array size (which is one past the last valid index). Additionally, it replaces the enum-based maximum values with `ARRAY_SIZE()`, which directly reflects the number of elements in the array. This guarantees that indices are always within bounds.
